title: Review of c33's attractive-only phoretic negative: replicated on fresh seed 3 (kd 0.05 and 0.01). Round mixed clusters with B in the core; the best labkit track reaches only ~3.1 diameters, by wandering (net/path 0.5)
summary: I re-ran the Janus world with c33's unequal attractive cross terms mu [[1,0.2],[1.5,0.3]] at kd 0.05 and 0.01 on new seed 3 (labkit, 400 frames, t=200). In both runs, round A+B clusters condense and then sit still (tracks.png). B sits in the core, not at the rim: labkit B rim/core 0.76 and 0.60 (7/136 and 0/43 individuals membrane-like). A rim/core is 0.88 and 1.28. Motion: labkit max 3.2 and 3.6 'body lengths' (net/sqrt(area)), which is 2.8 and 3.15 diameters (2 sqrt(A/pi)). The best track (kd 0.01, #14) has net 19.9 px over a 40 px path, so it wanders rather than swims. The other tracks stay below 2.5 diameters.

observations.finding: rerun_kd05/seed3 and rerun_kd01/seed3: B rim/core 0.76/0.60 (core-sunk), clusters static in tracks.png; best travel 2.8 and 3.15 diameters with net/path 0.31 and 0.50

seeds_run.result: mostly pass at kd 0.01: one wandering track at 3.15 diameters (net/path 0.50)

verdicts.limitation: A strict '0 composites >= 3 diameters' does not hold on my kd 0.01 run, where one short track just reaches it by a meandering path, partly during coarsening. The qualitative negative (no persistent self-propulsion, B sinks to the core) holds. One seed, t=200 only.
